classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal radii and use them to identify isosceles triangles.

content.prompt: Identify the isosceles triangles in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Circle with centre O above horizontal chord AB; radii OA and OB complete triangle AOB. Ordinary source strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: A and B lie on the circle centred at O. OA and OB are radii. No numerical angle or length is given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and point labels are visible; triangle identification is stored in the answer.

answer.worked: $OA=OB$ because both are radii of the same circle. Therefore $\triangle AOB$ is isosceles.

spec.description: Circle centred at O, with C upper left, A lower left and B lower right. CA is vertical, AB horizontal, and diameter CB passes through O. Segment AO is drawn.
spec.mathematics: OA, OB and OC are radii. CB is a straight segment through O. The schematic appearance supplies no additional equal-length or right-angle givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Point labels and supplied segments only; no answer names or equality marks are added.

answer.worked: $OA=OB=OC$ because they are radii of the same circle. Thus $\triangle AOB$ and $\triangle COA$ each have two equal sides and are isosceles.

spec.description: Triangle ABC inscribed in a circle centred at O, with A at the top, B at the right and C lower left. All three radii are drawn. Source blue chords, purple radii and grey circumference become ordinary black geometry.
spec.mathematics: OA, OB and OC are equal radii, dividing triangle ABC into triangles AOB, BOC and AOC.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied chords, radii, centre marker and point labels remain visible; triangle identifications appear only in answers.

answer.worked: $OA=OB=OC$ because they are radii of the same circle. Each of $\triangle AOB$, $\triangle BOC$ and $\triangle AOC$ contains two of these radii, so each is isosceles.
